title: Ball method: first effective leprosy treatment
summary: Chemist Alice Ball made chaulmoogra oil injectable, producing the first effective treatment for leprosy before her death at 24.
why: The only effective leprosy treatment until sulfonamide drugs in the 1940s.

notes.problem: 'Used worldwide until antibiotics' not in source; source: 'the only available, effective treatment for leprosy' until sulfonamides in the 1940s.

unsung.contribution: Turned chaulmoogra oil into an injectable form, the first effective leprosy treatment.
unsung.recognition: After her death, Arthur Dean published the work without crediting her; others restored her credit later.
